title: Images shipped a stale binary: Buildroot caches the local package source
description: The BeagleBone booted and printed version=bc7af0d-dirty, a binary from 2026-11-19, while every image built that day reported nothing else: Buildroot treats WA_TRANSCRIBER_SITE=prebuilt with SITE_METHOD=local as immutable, so build/wa-transcriber-local kept the first rsync and the install step never ran again. os/prebuilt was refreshed but never used. Fix: the rpi2/bbb targets run wa-transcriber-dirclean before building, and $(GO_DIST) now depends on the Go sources so dist/ cannot stay stale either. Verified by grepping the version string out of sdcard.img.
close_reason: dirclean + source deps; S01data mounts the device and heals once

title: /dev/root: /boot and /data were never mounted on the images
description: First boot on a BeagleBone Black (2026-11-20) showed the binary looping on 'open session db: failed to upgrade database: ... unable to open database file', and no ttyACM0 despite console=usb. Cause: S00boot and S01data read the root device from field 1 of /proc/mounts, where the kernel calls it /dev/root, so both fell into the 'cannot tell the SD card' branch and exited. /data was never created (hence the sqlite error) and /boot was never mounted (hence wat.txt was unread and S02console saw no console= line). Fix: shared /usr/lib/wat/sd.sh resolves the device through /sys/dev/block/<major>:<minor> from /proc/self/mountinfo, with the root= argument as fallback, and both scripts use it; check.sh gains a unit test for the mapping and fails if any init script parses /proc/mounts again.
close_reason: sd.sh resolves the root device via /sys/dev/block; both scripts use it

title: M11: the eMMC boot partitions are never written, so the ROM boots the old bootloader
description: Found on the board: after a verified clone (MBR + p1..p3, every region read back identical) the BeagleBone Black does not boot from the eMMC with the SD removed - no USB gadget, no network, so it dies before userspace. The AM335x ROM reads EXT_CSD PARTITION_CONFIG and, when it selects a boot partition, loads MLO from /dev/mmcblk1boot0 (present on this board), which the install never touches: it still holds the stock Debian SPL, which then finds no kernel for its layout. Needs: read EXT_CSD (mmc-utils or the MMC_IOC_CMD ioctl) and either set BOOT_PARTITION_ENABLE to the user area or write MLO/u-boot into boot0/boot1 at the offsets the ROM and SPL expect; add both to the plan and REPORT them; verify with a real power-off, card out, boot. The install must not say 'bootable' from a read-back alone - it has to check the boot path the ROM will take. Also needs mmc-utils in the image if we go that way.
notes: Wrong diagnosis: boot0 is empty and the ROM does use the user area (it got as far as loading the kernel). The real cause: the clone copied the card's boot file verbatim and it names root=/dev/mmcblk0p2; booted from the eMMC that is mmcblk1p2, so the kernel panicked before userspace (no network, no USB gadget) - which is why the board looked dead. Fixed in the install (repointBoot, before the marker, reported on the console) and pinned by TestInstallRepointsTheBootFile. Closed as fixed; the remaining step is the physical power-cycle proof, tracked in wat-3h4.4.

title: M10: U-Boot bootcounter so a bad kernel also falls back
description: The userspace gate covers an image whose app never becomes healthy; it cannot cover a kernel or init that never reaches userspace. The image's U-Boot already has BOOTCOUNT_LIMIT, BOOTCOUNT_AM33XX, ENV_IS_IN_FAT and CMD_EXT4_WRITE (checked in os/_output/bbb/build/uboot-custom/.config), with bootlimit=0: set bootlimit=3 and altbootcmd (switch the boot file back and boot), have the updater set upgrade_available=1 before switching and the 60 s health timer clear it with fw_setenv (uboot-tools + /etc/fw_env.config pointing at the FAT env file), and prove it by flashing a slot whose kernel panics. Needs the console, so it goes after the first flash of the two-slot layout. Pi 2 has no U-Boot env of this kind: document its own mechanism or accept the loss there.

title: M11: verify by read-back, then docs and field test
description: Compare the written regions against the card before saying 'remove the SD and reboot'; on a mismatch say the eMMC is not bootable yet (the card still is). README 'install to internal flash' + ARCHITECTURE note. Field test on the BBB: install, power off, remove the card, boot from eMMC paired; an M10 image update from the eMMC; a power cut during the install then re-run.
notes:
2026-11-22: code done (internal/flash + -flash + card + wat-migrate in S01data, os/check.sh asserts the section). The eMMC write has NOT been exercised: needs the console and the owner's go-ahead, since it is their internal flash. Everything before the first byte is checked and a failed clone leaves the card bootable.
2026-11-22, on the board: clone writes 352 MB and every region reads back identical; the session (config.json, session.db, -wal, -shm) is now staged on the eMMC's boot partition and verified present; no mount is left behind so a second install runs. Three bugs found and fixed: the staging temp name used a colon (illegal on VFAT, EINVAL, nothing staged), the kernel's stale partition table needed partx -u before mounting <target>p1, and the cleanup only remounted read-only (with swapped arguments) instead of detaching, which left the boot partition mounted and the next install refusing. Remaining: the physical step - power off, remove the SD, boot from eMMC - which only the owner can do; then S01data creates p4 and copies the staged files.
Also fixed after the first eMMC boot failed: the clone copied the card's boot file verbatim (root=/dev/mmcblk0p2), so the kernel panicked before userspace when booting from the eMMC (mmcblk1p2) - the board looked dead. The install now repoints root= on the target's boot file (reported on the console, tested). Verified on the board: the eMMC's boot file says root=/dev/mmcblk1p2, rest byte-identical, no mounts left. Remaining: the physical power-cycle proof with the card out.
2026-11-23: the eMMC boots. Owner powered on with the SD removed; over ttyACM0: root=/dev/mmcblk1p2, USB console up, http://192.168.15.51/healthz = 200. Next session must look at the /data migration, which looks PARTIAL: /boot/wat-migrate.d still exists (config.json, session.db) and /data has session.db* but NO config.json, so S01data copied some files and then neither finished nor cleaned up. Read dmesg | grep S01data on the eMMC, find the reason, fix, then the device comes up with its settings. Also left to prove: the A/B switch on the eMMC (mirror the SD test with mmcblk1p3).
2026-11-23, resolved on the board: the eMMC boot + migration now work end to end. After fixing the two S01data bugs (mountpoint guard when /data is already up; remove the marker only after /boot is remounted rw, checking each removal) the staged session was copied into /data (config.json + session.db*), the marker and staged dir were removed, and after a reboot the device still runs from the eMMC with the migrated settings (the UI asks for the migrated password instead of the setup page). Note the flashed image predates these two fixes - they are in the next image. Remaining for M11: nothing functional; the A/B switch on the eMMC is the M10 item.

title: M11: clone mode (-flash and a System page button behind a typed confirmation)
description: Writes this card's image to the eMMC: MLO/U-Boot, boot partition, root slot, fresh DATA partition, all read from the SD card so it works offline. Progress on the console (the UI does not survive) and in the log buffer; repeatable after a power cut because the card is intact.

title: M11: identify the eMMC target by rule and refuse when ambiguous
description: The block device whose /sys/block/*/device/type is MMC, that is not the device the running root came from, with its size; refuse when ambiguous and print the candidates. Refuse with one line on a board without internal flash (Pi 2).

title: M10: release job attaches the images, field test on both boards
description: Release workflow builds and attaches both board images, wat-manifest writes the images block. Field test: update over the network, /data untouched, 10 random power cuts during write/flip/health, a deliberately broken image falls back, old-layout refusal. Record in docs/STATUS.md.
notes: 2026-11-22: wat-manifest writes the images block when beagle.img/rpi2.img are in dist/, and both images build with the A/B table (369099264 bytes each, sha256 in docs/STATUS.md). The workflow still uploads only binaries; attaching the images and the field test are open.

title: M10: bootloader slot choice and boot counter (BBB uEnv.txt, Pi 2 config/cmdline)
description: Prove by hand on both consoles before writing Go: uEnv.txt on the BeagleBone Black selects the root slot and the counter file, the Pi 2 equivalent (config.txt/cmdline.txt), three unconfirmed starts fall back to the other slot, and the counter is writable from the running system (FAT boot partition, mounted briefly or written through a small helper). Record the exact file formats in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 11.
notes: 2026-11-22: the slot choice is the root= token in the boot file, rewritten atomically by internal/imageupdate (extlinux.conf on the BBB, cmdline.txt on the Pi 2); the layout file /etc/wat/image.json ships per board and os/check.sh asserts it. The boot counter half is wat-kfd.6 (U-Boot bootlimit/altbootcmd), which still needs the console.

title: M10: internal/imageupdate — write the inactive slot, verify by read-back, flip, health gate
description: Download to /data (space checked against the image size first), stream into the inactive partition while hashing, fsync, read back and compare, then flip the boot file and clear the counter; never touch the running slot or /data. Manifest gains images:{beagle,rpi2} with file/sha256/size and a layout version; a device on the old table refuses with one line. Reuse the signature verification, the atomic write and the 60 s health timer from internal/update. Tests with a file-backed fake device and a fake boot partition.

title: M10: partition layout with two root slots
description: p1 boot (FAT), p2 root A, p3 root B (both ext4 ro), p4 data. genimage configs for both boards, mkimage.sh, S01data (DATA is already found by label, check it tolerates the new index), os/check.sh asserts the layout, both images build and boot from the console. This is the one step that costs every existing device a reflash.

title: M10 — Image (OS) updates in place: two root slots
description: D18: the OS updates by writing the inactive of two root slots; the FAT boot partition holds the slot choice and the boot counter; /data is never touched, so an image update never costs a re-pairing. Costs one reflash because the partition table changes. Details and exit criteria: docs/PLAN.md M10. Needs the M9 key and a v1.1 image to start.

title: M9: install must survive a slow link (timeout, progress, free space)
description: Found while reading the code after the board run. internal/web/update.go wraps every button in a 60 s context, so the 24 MB asset is cancelled after 60 s on anything slower than ~3.5 Mbit/s: over ethernet it took 12 s, on a weak WiFi dongle (the M5b setup) it would fail every time. Give the install its own, much longer budget (or none, with a cancel button), keep 30-60 s for check only, and say in the card that a download can take minutes. Also: no free-space check before the download (a nearly full /data fails mid-write with a confusing error: check statfs for the asset size + slack and refuse early), and no progress feedback while it downloads (the page just spins; the log has the sizes, the card should too). Deterministic tests with a slow httptest handler and a fake statfs seam.
notes: 2026-11-22/23: the timeouts are now per action (check 60 s, binary install 10 min, image install 20 min - a 160 MB image over WiFi no longer dies at 60 s), the image installer already refused a slot smaller than the image, and the binary installer checks the free space in /data before the first byte with an injectable FreeSpace seam (test: refuses without downloading anything). Progress in the card is still only the log line at start/end; a per-MB progress line during the download is not done.

title: M9: field test on Pi 2 and BeagleBone Black (owner)
description: Owner-only, on hardware. Update over WiFi from the current release to the next one; kill -9 during the download and during the install; power cut during the install; a deliberately broken binary (same version, return 1 in main) rolled back after three tries with last_failure visible; manual rollback restoring config.json/session.db; update right after a reflash so the factory binary is newer; at most three binaries in /data/bin. Record the results in docs/STATUS.md (device, versions, what was sent to the phone).
notes: 2026-11-22, agent, BeagleBone Black over ttyACM0 with a throwaway key and manifests served from the LAN (data dir /data/wat-test, the paired session untouched): check, install (24 MB, sha256+ELF, exec, promoted, healthy after 60 s), automatic rollback of a broken v0.3.0 after three tries with last_failure in the UI, kill -9 mid-download (no pending, .part pruned at boot), retention and exec-from-/data all pass. Details in docs/STATUS.md. Two bugs found and fixed: GOARM from build tags (every board install failed) and the 1 h cache hiding a fresh release (Checker.Refresh). Still to do here: the flashed image needs -update-dir/-bootstrap and a reflash, the Pi 2, power cuts during an install, and the owner's real key (wat-t3l.5).

title: M9: config + System page card + i18n for updates
description: config.Store: update_check (off|daily, default off = the opt-in daily check) and update_auto (bool, default false), env overrides WAT_UPDATE_CHECK/WAT_UPDATE_AUTO, validation + tests, never persisted env values (D10). internal/web: a System page card (current version, build time, 'Check for updates', 'v0.3.0 available' + notes link, 'Install and restart', 'Back to v0.1.1', last rollback reason) behind s.auth with the existing Origin check; handlers POST /system/update/check, /system/update/install, /system/update/rollback; the card is hidden when the update dir is empty (Docker) and the install button warns while a note is queued or transcribing; the daily timer (off unless update_check=daily) plus update_auto live in one place and are visible as a setting. Define the small interface the card needs (Checker/Installer/Rollback/Status) in internal/web so main can pass the *update.Service. Strings in internal/bot/i18n.go en+it with the completeness test. No hardware, no network in tests: fakes only.

title: M9: bootstrap in main + inittab flag + os check
description: Wire internal/update into cmd/wa-transcriber: flag -update-dir (env WAT_UPDATE_DIR, empty = off, Docker and dev machines), run the boot decision at the very top of run() before logbuf/config/WhatsApp and skip it for -version/-healthcheck; exec the returned Action.Path (syscall.Exec with os.Args/os.Environ()), and change restart() to exec the bootstrap path (a -bootstrap flag or the value recorded at startup) instead of os.Executable(); log the rollback/promotion at WARN with the version; set verified+tries=0 on a 60s timer; snapshot config.json+session.db into /data/rollback/<version>/ before the first exec of a new version and restore it on rollback. Pass the *update.Service to web.Options (see wat-t3l.4 for the interface it must satisfy). os/board/common/rootfs-overlay/etc/inittab passes -update-dir /data/bin and os/check.sh asserts it; docs note in ARCHITECTURE 7 (networking/services) if the line changes. Unit tests with a temp dir and an injected exec func.

title: M9: release side — manifest.json, wat-sign/wat-keygen, pubkey injection
description: tools/wat-manifest (reads dist/, a version and the tag, writes manifest.json per the epic design), tools/wat-sign (ed25519 detached signature, base64 on one line, -key path outside the repo), tools/wat-keygen (generates a keypair, refuses to overwrite, prints the base64 public key). release/update-pubkey.txt holds the public key (empty today with a comment: the owner generates it) and the Makefile passes -X main.updatePubKey=<contents> in LDFLAGS so an empty file compiles self-update out; same for the os/Makefile prebuilt copy. .github/workflows/release.yml generates and uploads manifest.json; a make sign-manifest target downloads it from the release, signs it and uploads manifest.json.ed25519 with gh. Test tools/wat-manifest with the repo's own test style (a temp dist dir), keep go vet clean.

title: M9: internal/update — manifest, signature, slots, install, check
description: New package internal/update, stdlib only (no go.mod change): ParseManifest/AssetKey/CheckExecutable(debug/elf)/Compare+IsUpgrade/VerifyManifest(ed25519 over the raw manifest bytes)/LoadState+SaveState (atomic, like config.Store)/Boot decision (promote pending -> active, rollback to previous when tries>3 or the sha256 differs, newer factory beats older active, prune stray files and .part)/Install (download to .part with a size cap and sha256 tee, verify, fsync, rename, fsync dir, then state)/Checker (GET the two URLs, verify, 1h cache in memory + on disk). No wiring into main or web yet, no exec in the package: Boot returns an Action{Path} the caller execs. Table-driven tests with httptest and t.TempDir: promote, rollback, prune, tampered binary, wrong arch, unsigned/bad signature, truncated download, state pointing at a missing file.

title: M9 — Binary updates from GitHub releases (boards only)
description: D17: the binary updates itself from GitHub releases. Runtime binary lives in /data/bin with three slots (active, previous, pending); the read-only factory binary in /usr/bin is the bootstrap and can never be broken. Exec of the bootstrap is the restart; a try counter and a session.db snapshot turn a crash loop into an automatic rollback. Docker is out (feature off when -update-dir is empty). Details: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, docs/PLAN.md M9.
design:
Contract for M9 (D17). The release ships, next to the three binaries and
SHA256SUMS, a manifest and a detached ed25519 signature of it:

  manifest.json           (asset, generated on tags)
  manifest.json.ed25519   (asset, signed offline by the owner, base64 of the
                          64-byte signature on one line)

manifest.json:

  {"schema": 1,
   "version": "v0.2.0",
   "released_at": "2026-11-21T10:00:00Z",
   "notes_url": "https://github.com/emdioh/wa-transcriber/releases/tag/v0.2.0",
   "min_from": "v0.1.0",
   "assets": {
     "linux-armv7":  {"file": "wa-transcriber-linux-armv7",  "sha256": "<64 hex>", "size": 23456789},
     "linux-arm64":  {"file": "wa-transcriber-linux-arm64",  "sha256": "<64 hex>", "size": 23456789},
     "linux-amd64":  {"file": "wa-transcriber-linux-amd64",  "sha256": "<64 hex>", "size": 23456789}}}

"min_from" is empty when there is no constraint; a device running an older
version than min_from refuses the update (its state format is too old).

Check URL (a CDN GET, no GitHub API, no token, redirects followed):
  https://github.com/emdioh/wa-transcriber/releases/latest/download/manifest.json
  .../manifest.json.ed25519

Arch key: runtime.GOARCH/GOARM -> "linux-armv7" (arm, GOARM 7),
"linux-arm64", "linux-amd64"; anything else is unsupported (no update).

Version compare is semver-ish over `git describe` shapes: v1.2.3,
v1.2.3-4-gabc123 (four commits after the tag: newer than v1.2.3, older than
v1.2.4), and "dev" which is treated as newer than everything (a dev build
never offers to downgrade itself to a release).

On-disk state (/data/bin):
  state.json                 {schema, active, previous, pending, tries,
                              verified, last_failure:{version,reason,at}}
  wa-transcriber-<version>   at most three files
  /data/updates/*.part       transient
  /data/rollback/<version>/  config.json + session.db snapshot

Boot order (bootstrap = the read-only factory binary, everything above runs
before logging/config/WhatsApp): pending (promote, then exec) -> active
(rollback when tries > 3 or the hash fails, else exec) -> run the factory
binary. A newer factory binary beats an older active slot.

Restart = syscall.Exec(bootstrap path), never os.Executable() and never
exit+respawn. Verified is set 60 s after start, not at start.

title: M6: confirm pairing on a board after the QR-handler fix
description:
Owner step (needs the board + a phone). Flash or deploy a build that contains the wat-f2z.8 fix, then pair from the phone.

Expected in the log: at most one 'pairing attempt ended' line before the network is up, one 'scan the QR code' line, then the phone links the device ('paired jid=...'). The QR must stay usable for its full minute and refresh twice more (20 s each) if nobody scans; no 'Error sending close to websocket' after the QR appears.

Before the fix the phone answered 'cannot pair' and the log showed that websocket close 363 ms after the QR. Serial console: /dev/ttyACM0 at 115200 with a login prompt; the app logs to the web UI /logs page.
acceptance_criteria: A phone links the device on the first scan; the QR refreshes while unused; the log shows a single QR per attempt and no websocket-close warning right after it.
notes: 2026-11-21: the fixed binary (v0.1.1-23-gfcada57, sha256 3512d440...) is installed and running on the board (BBE 192.168.15.43, /usr/bin/wa-transcriber, pid changes only on restart). Verified over the gadget console: /proc/<pid>/exe hashes to it, one ESTABLISHED WhatsApp socket that survives code rotation (one planned reconnect per ~160 s code set, new ephemeral port, same pid). Only the phone scan is left.
close_reason: Owner paired a phone on the board on 2026-11-21: the device linked on the first scan of the new QR.

title: Pairing: failed attempt leaves a stale QR handler that kills the socket
description:
A connect attempt that fails after GetQRChannel leaves a whatsmeow event handler registered with an already cancelled context (whatsmeow removes the handler only when the QR channel closes). The next attempt's QR event reaches that stale handler, whose emitter takes the ctx.Done branch and calls client.Disconnect(): the socket dies right after the QR is shown, the phone scans a dead code and reports 'cannot pair', and since the disconnect is expected there is no event and no auto-reconnect.

Seen on the board at 10:40: the first attempt failed on DNS (network not up), the retry showed a QR at 25.019 and whatsmeow logged 'Error sending close to websocket: EOF' 363 ms later. Reproduced on amd64: QR at +0.00 s, socket dead at +0.03 s, connected=false forever, no Disconnected event.

Fixed by caching one QR channel per pairing session (qrChanCache) so a failed attempt reuses it instead of registering a second handler.
acceptance_criteria: A failed first connect followed by a successful second connect leaves the client connected and the QR valid (probe on amd64); unit tests cover channel reuse, error paths and cancellation.

title: Verify wired DHCP on a board after the first-poll fix
description: The managed manager never ran udhcpc on a booted interface: carrier reads 0 while the link is down and nothing lifted it, so Ethernet.Up() was never called (no ip link set up, no udhcpc). Fixed in internal/netmgr/linux.go: the first poll always runs the up path, with regression test TestManagedFirstPollDrivesEthernetWithCarrierDown. Needs the owner: make -C os bbb, flash os/_output/bbb/images/sdcard.img, boot with a cable, expect a DHCP address on eth0 and 'ethernet: dhcp lease' in the log; repeat with make -C os rpi2.

comments.author: emdioh
comments.text: Wired DHCP is now confirmed on the BeagleBone Black (part of this bead's criteria): a cold boot of a build at edded8d brought eth0 up on the first poll and logged 'ethernet: carrier up first=true' + 'ethernet: dhcp lease', landing 192.168.15.51/20 and keeping it across a later carrier blip. The rpi2 half of this bead is still open.

title: /data mount fails on LABEL=DATA even when the label exists
description: Second boot on the board: mmcblk0 had p1 p2 p3, S01data reached its mount step and failed with 'LABEL=DATA: Can't open blockdev' / 'No such file or directory'. The tag lookup goes through blkid and did not resolve even though blkid itself reported the label, so S01data now mounts $datadev directly with -t ext4, logs the type and label it found, leaves a foreign filesystem alone instead of formatting over it, and retries the mount once after e2fsck -p. Also put /var/lib on tmpfs (seedrng could not write there) and made the mount step loud via /dev/kmsg.
close_reason: dirclean + source deps; S01data mounts the device and heals once

title: /boot is never mounted: wat.txt is ignored on the images
description: The binary reads /boot/wat.txt for setup_ap_key, country and the mDNS name (internal/netmgr/ap.go WatTxtPath). Nothing mounts the FAT boot partition: the common fstab has no /boot entry, /boot does not even exist in the target, and no init script mounts it. Result on a flashed card: the setup AP falls back to wa-setup-<MAC>, the country and hostname lines do nothing, and the README/Flashing section tells users to edit a file that is never read. Fix: mount partition 1 read-only at /boot from an early init script, after creating the mountpoint in post-build.sh.
close_reason: Image: /boot mounted, ttyS0 cmdline, opt-in console= getty

title: Verify backup and restore on the board
description: Backup/restore merged (a619933) but never run on hardware. On the BBB: download a backup from the System page, check the tar lists manifest.json first and the four/five state files with matching sha256; factory-reset the device; restore the archive from the setup page; confirm it comes back with the old password, the paired session and the API key, and that the archive with a flipped byte is refused without touching /data. Also check the size of a real archive (session.db + WAL) against the 64 MB cap.
notes: 2026-11-23, on the BBB with a throwaway instance (real binary v0.1.1-64-ge960b64, own data dir, session copied from /data): GET /system/backup returns a 5.9 kB tar.gz, manifest.json first (schema 1, version, per-file size+sha256) then config.json (0600) and session.db/-wal/-shm; the hashes match the extracted files. A tampered archive is refused with HTTP 400 on both POST /system/restore and POST /restore and the device's config is unchanged (same sha256 before/after). Setup-mode restore (the reflash case) works end to end: fresh data dir -> setup page -> POST /restore with the good archive -> 'Restarting' -> the device comes back with the API key restored in config.json, the session files back, and / redirecting to /login (password restored). Real archive size 5.9 kB against the 64 MB cap; not exercised with a large session or a WiFi file (none saved on this device).

title: Tools: a serial console runner that returns when the command does, not after a quiet period
description: tools/serial-run.sh waits for the line to go quiet before it decides an answer is complete, so every call costs seconds even when the command is instant, and its -t is a wall-clock timeout rather than an event. Write tools/serialrun (Go, stdlib only): one open fd for the whole session, raw tty, markers around the command, stream every line as it arrives and exit the moment the END marker appears with the command's exit status. No fixed sleeps: prompt and login are detected by their own text; an idle timeout only fires when the console has been silent (configurable), and it says what it saw. Keep the shell version for reference.
notes: Delivered as tools/serialrun: event-driven (one fd, raw tty, wake CR, login/password/shell prompts detected by text, marker-framed command, exits the moment the END tag parses). stdout carries only the command's output once; -verbose shows the console's side; the whole call is bounded by -timeout (15s default, raise it for long commands) with -idle/-prompt defaulting to it. Measured on the board: echo 0.01s; a 3x sleep loop streams tick 1/2/3 and ends 3.0s in; -timeout 3s on a 20s command gives up at 3.0s with one line. Two board-found bugs fixed: getty's 'wa login: ' has a trailing space so the login state never fired, and a command calling exit kills the frame shell (exit 2 is correct; use false or sh -c 'exit 7' for statuses).

title: Backup and restore of the device state (so a reflash needs no re-pairing)
description: Download one archive from the web UI (config.json, session.db with -wal/-shm, wifi.json, plus a manifest with sizes and sha256) and upload it back after a reflash: the setup page accepts it while no password is set, the System page when logged in. Restore verifies the manifest and every hash before writing anything, writes through temp names, then restarts. Refuses a foreign, truncated or unknown-schema archive; the archive holds secrets (API key, session, WiFi PSK) so it is only ever served to an authenticated session, never logged, and the UI says so.
notes:
Note: the commit landed on main (a619933), not isolated on the backup-restore worktree branch as intended; the branch points at the same commit. Feature exists (internal/backup + GET /system/backup, POST /system/restore, POST /restore in setup mode) and the suite is green, but nobody reviewed the code or exercised it on a device yet. The update work was the priority, so this stays open for review.
Merged into main by the owner (a619933 was already in main's history); the backup-restore worktree and branch are removed. Code reviewed at a high level only: internal/backup + GET /system/backup, POST /system/restore, POST /restore in setup mode, suite green. NOT exercised on a device yet - see the follow-up bead.

title: Web: reset everything from the login page when the password is lost and nothing is paired
description: Losing the password and the phone left no way in: !password/!reset need the chat, the UI needs the password. POST /reset (unauthenticated) is offered and accepted only while WA.Paired() is false, requires the typed RESET, logs at WARN, and does what !reset does. On a linked device the page does not render it and the route says to use the chat, so a working device cannot be erased from the LAN. Tests: shown/hidden by pairing, confirmation required, foreign Origin refused, no password -> setup page. ARCHITECTURE section 5.

title: M10: the System card says 'no image installed' for a slot it did not write itself
description: Found on the board after switching slots by hand: /data/image-boot.json does not exist, so the card shows 'Other slot: slot A · no image installed' although slot A holds a valid root filesystem (it is the one we booted from a minute earlier). SlotState only knows about switches this process performed. Fix: probe the partition — read the ext4 superblock (magic 0xEF53 at 1024+56) and its volume label (1024+120) and report 'empty' vs 'an image is here, version unknown', which is also what a reflashed card and a hand switch need. Cheap (a 1 KB read) and testable with a temp file.

title: M11: migrate /data so the device stays paired
description: Create DATA on the eMMC, copy config.json, session.db* and wifi.json from the running /data (reuse the M9 snapshot code), verify with sha256. Without this an install to eMMC costs a re-pairing, which is the main reason to do it at all.

title: M11 — Install from the SD card to the BeagleBone Black eMMC
description: The BBB has 4 GB eMMC and SD cards die. Clone the running card onto the eMMC, migrate /data so the device stays paired, verify before declaring success (a half-written eMMC is simply not bootable yet, the card still is). Layout identical to M10, so binary and image updates work there unchanged. Details: docs/PLAN.md M11. Needs M10 first.

title: M10: System page card for the image, daily check and update_auto coverage
description: A 'System image' card: slot in use, other slot bootable or not, available image, 'install and reboot', 'back to the previous image'; on the old layout the card shows 'reflash once to enable image updates' and hides the button. The existing daily check and update_auto cover images too, but never automatically install an image while a note is queued.
notes: 2026-11-22: the System page card, the handlers and the image service are in and tested (internal/web/image.go). NOT done from this bead: the daily check and update_auto do not look at image entries yet (cmd/wa-transcriber/update.go only handles the binary manifest), so an image is offered on the card but never installed by the timer.

title: Docs: README section on updates (owner-facing)
description: README has nothing about updates: how the card works, that the device only ever runs current+previous+next, that a failed update rolls back by itself, that the release must be signed with the offline key (make sign-manifest) or devices refuse it, and that the update directory is only wired in the image (Docker and dev builds are unaffected). Keep it short, in the style of the existing Flashing section.

title: M9: !update command in the self chat
description: The i18n strings exist (msgUpdate* in internal/bot/i18n.go, added with the System card) but nothing uses them. Add a bot.Updater interface and the commands: '!update' shows the current version, the automatic-check setting and any available release (checking on demand, with the 1 h cache); '!update install' asks for a confirmation within 60 s like '!reset' and then stages and restarts; '!update rollback' likewise. Self chat only (D6), no secrets involved. This is also the way the owner updates from a phone when the UI password is not at hand. Tests with a fake updater; main wires the same service the web card uses.

title: M9: owner — generate and store the update signing keypair
description: Owner-only: run 'go run ./tools/wat-keygen -out ~/wat-update.key' (or the equivalent once wat-t3l.1 lands), keep the private key OFF the repository and backed up (it is the only thing that can sign an update a device will accept: lose it and every device needs a reflash), paste the printed base64 public key into release/update-pubkey.txt and commit. Rotating the key later needs a release signed with the old key (or a reflash), so back it up.

title: Web UI: show the saved API key, make the log refresh visible
description: Owner report: pasting an API key into the Transcription page leaves the field empty afterwards (it is a password input with an empty value and the placeholder 'saved: leave empty to keep it'), so there is no way to confirm what is stored; and ticking 'Refresh every 5 s' on the Logs page appears to do nothing. Causes: the field never renders the stored key; the checkbox only did location.reload(), which is invisible when no new lines exist, and /static/ was served with no Cache-Control or validators (embed.FS has a zero modtime), so a stale app.js could stick. Fix: prefill the key as visible text (env-provided keys stay hidden and disabled), poll a new GET /logs/live (no-store, honouring ?level=) every 5 s and show an 'updated HH:MM:SS' stamp plus the line count, and serve /static/ with no-cache plus a version query so an upgrade always wins.
close_reason: Implemented and tested: field prefilled as visible text (env keys stay hidden), GET /logs/live + 5 s polling with a visible timestamp and line count, /static/ served no-cache with a version query. Gate: gofmt, go vet, go test -race all pass.

title: App respawn-looped ~1/s for 60-90 s on two of four boots
description: On the BeagleBone Black the app started and exited within about a second, ~1/s, for 60-90 s after two boots (syslog: 144 and 111 'starting pid ... / exited' pairs), while the other two boots showed 0 restarts (app pid 265/460, stable). The two looping boots ran a binary built from an uncommitted intermediate tree (md5 6c384d6a..., before the udhcpc-script fix was committed); the two clean boots ran a build of edded8d (version v0.1.1-31-gedded8d). Not enough evidence to call it a code bug: the app's stderr goes to /dev/console, which is not the USB console, so the exit reason was never captured. /data was mounted exactly once on the clean boot (no double mount) and /etc/fstab has LABEL=DATA with noauto, so the 'resolved mount race' theory does not apply. Next step: keep the app's log visible (see the log-visibility bead) and watch whether M6's 50 power cuts reproduce it; if it does, read the first stderr line of the first failed start.

title: The app's log is invisible on a board: stderr goes to /dev/console, not the USB console
description: On the BeagleBone Black the app writes to /dev/console, which is not the USB gadget tty (S02console's getty on ttyGS0), so its startup errors, panics and connection state are lost: /tmp/messages only has init's own lines, and the Logs page needs a login. Diagnosing wat-f2z.9/f2z.10 and the boot crash loop needed a hand-edited inittab ('::respawn:/bin/sh -c "exec /usr/bin/wa-transcriber ... >>/tmp/app.log 2>&1"') to see anything at all, which is what finally showed 'connected to WhatsApp' and the full startup sequence. Fix: ship that redirection in the inittab overlay (or add a -log file flag / a syslog sink), so a boot-time failure is inspectable without a console hack. Also note /tmp is tmpfs, so use a path that survives long enough to read or copy it before reboot.

title: mDNS: confirm wa.local resolves from an Android phone
description: The responder fixes are deployed on the BeagleBone Black by hand (0.0.0.0:5353 bound, unicast one-shot queries answered conventionally, no self-rename) and verified from the dev box with tools/mdns-probe.py, but the original symptom was 'the phone cannot reach wa.local'. Needs the owner: on the iPhone/Android that failed, load http://wa.local/ on the LAN, and also try http://<board-ip>/ to prove the device itself is up. Report what the browser says for each. Android older than 12 with no Play System Update cannot resolve .local at all, so note the Android version if it fails.

title: S02console: the debug getty can be lost until reboot
description: After the board rebooted around 12:53 the USB gadget console never came back: /dev/ttyACM0 re-enumerated but stays silent, so there is no login prompt and no way to log in until the board is power-cycled. S02console waits for /dev/ttyGS0 in a bounded loop (`while [ ! -c /dev/ttyGS0 ] && [ "$i" -lt 25 ]`) and gives up for good when the gadget appears later than that, which is exactly what a reboot with a client attached can do. Look at the loop: keep retrying, or respawn the getty when the tty appears. Seen on the BeagleBone Black after a reboot: HTTP keeps working but the console is dead.
acceptance_criteria: A reboot with the USB cable attached always ends with a login prompt on the gadget console, however late ttyGS0 appears.
notes: 2026-11-21: observed live. After the gadget re-enumerated, /dev/ttyACM0 existed but stayed silent for roughly ten minutes; then the login prompt came back on its own, no reboot needed. So the loop is still alive, it just takes far longer than the 25 x 1 s it looks like it waits, or the getty starts and the prompt is not flushed until a client writes. Worth measuring from the serial console after a reboot: how long until 'wa login:' answers.

title: netmgr: carrier loss flushes the interface address and kills live sockets
description:
Ethernet.Down() runs 'ip addr flush dev <iface>' and is called on every carrier-down transition. Any open TCP connection bound to that address dies instantly: the WhatsApp websocket, an in-flight transcription upload, an mDNS socket. The board log shows a flap right after boot (carrier up first=true at 19.306, dhcp lease 22.650, carrier up first=false at 23.312, dhcp lease again 23.807), so a fresh boot can flush the address while a pairing socket is live.

Fix options: on carrier loss keep the address and only stop DHCP (re-run udhcpc when the carrier returns), or add a debounce before Down(). Flush only on explicit teardown (leaving managed mode, switching to AP mode).
acceptance_criteria: A carrier blip on the board does not drop an established TCP connection; the address survives a down/up cycle and only changes when DHCP returns a different lease.
close_reason: Fixed and proven on the BeagleBone Black: Ethernet.Down keeps the address (Flush is the explicit teardown) and the image ships its own idempotent udhcpc script (overlay, no-op deconfig, ip addr replace on bound). A wget download held open across a simulated carrier blip received all 10 post-blip lines and exited 0, the address stayed 192.168.15.51/20, the script logged 'deconfig on eth0: keeping address', and the WhatsApp socket never dropped (one 'connected to WhatsApp' line for the run). WiFi case still listed in STATUS.

title: Ship console=all in the images while validating boot and network
description: The user asked for the debug console to be on by default for the validation builds: wat.txt ships console=all (serial + USB CDC-ACM + HDMI getty), check.sh enforces it and os/README + STATUS say the passwordless root shell must be turned off (console=off) before a device is handed to anyone else.
close_reason: wat.txt ships console=all, checks and docs updated

title: Debug console in the images: console= in wat.txt
description: The images ship no login shell: BR2_TARGET_GENERIC_GETTY is off and the only getty line in inittab is commented out, so a serial header shows U-Boot and kernel messages and nothing else. Add an opt-in debug console chosen with console=off|serial|usb|both in wat.txt: a busybox getty on the board's UART (/dev/ttyS0 on the BeagleBone, /dev/ttyAMA0 on the Pi 2) and/or a CDC-ACM gadget over the USB client port through configfs (kernel has CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_ACM=y) with a getty on /dev/ttyGS0. Off by default; document that it gives a root shell with no password.
close_reason: Image: /boot mounted, ttyS0 cmdline, opt-in console= getty

title: BBB boot console uses ttyO0, Linux 6.1 calls the UART ttyS0
description: os/board/bbb/extlinux.conf passes console=ttyO0,115200. The omap-serial driver that created ttyO0 was removed in Linux 4.11; the kernel on this image is 6.1.46-bb.org and uses 8250_omap (CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_OMAP=y), which registers the port as ttyS0. So the kernel cmdline console matches no device and boot messages go nowhere. Fix the cmdline, and use ttyS0 for the debug getty on the BeagleBone (ttyAMA0 on the Pi 2, where ttyS0 is the mini UART).
close_reason: Image: /boot mounted, ttyS0 cmdline, opt-in console= getty

title: mDNS: send the unsolicited announcements on address change (M5 step 9)
description: PLAN.md M5 step 9 requires two unsolicited responses 1 s apart when an interface address changes. `mdns.Announce` (internal/netmgr/mdns/serve.go) implements exactly that and is unit-tested, but nothing calls it: `managed.serveMDNS` only answers queries via `mdns.Listen`, and nothing detects an address change. Effect: a client that resolved wa.local while the device was on the setup AP keeps the old IP until its 120 s TTL expires (queries for the new address still work). Wire it: remember the last address per interface in serveMDNS, call mdns.Announce on change, fake clock + table test in netmgr, and cover it in the M5b scenario that switches from AP to home WiFi.
close_reason: Listen now tracks per-interface addresses and announces twice on change

title: Turn coordination claims on by default

Once M2 says which variant is invisible, make it the default, update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (D-decisions on coordination) and docs/STATUS.md, and run the M3b field test: 20 notes from A, 20 from B, 20 from a third person → 0 duplicates / 0 missing, plus a run with B's instance stopped.

title: M2: experiment switch and probe sender/receiver (WAT_EXPERIMENTS=1)
description: No hardware needed. `internal/bot/experiment.go` + `internal/wa/experiment.go`: owner-only `!probe` sends V1–V6 ten seconds apart and logs `probe-tx variant=… id=…`; `wa.convert` logs `probe-rx variant=… field=… latency_ms=…` for reactions and the ContextInfo fields. Unreachable without the env switch so it can be deleted after the experiment.

title: M9: the release job never sets min_from
description: tools/wat-manifest writes min_from and both AllowUpgradeFrom and the Install handler enforce it (a device older than min_from is refused and told to update in steps), but .github/workflows/release.yml never passes -min-from, so it is always empty and the guard never fires. Decide the policy (e.g. min_from = the previous minor) and wire it in the release job, or drop the field.

title: mDNS: group join fails with EADDRINUSE and the name conflicts with itself
description: Board log: 'mdns: join group iface=eth0 err="setsockopt: address already in use"' immediately followed by 'mdns: name conflict, renamed old=wa.local new=wa-2.local'. Either the responder joins 239.255.255.250 twice on the same socket, or a previous responder (from an earlier carrier transition) is still bound, so the device answers its own probe and renames itself to wa-2.local. The name a user must type keeps changing across boots.
acceptance_criteria: A single responder per interface, no EADDRINUSE on carrier transitions, and the name stays wa.local on a network where no other host claims it.
close_reason: Fixed in internal/netmgr/mdns: own announcements (multicast loopback + LAN reflectors) no longer count as a conflict; the socket is bound wildcard so unicast queries (RFC 6762 s6.7) are answered and the double group join (EADDRINUSE) is gone. Unit tests added; on-board confirmation pending.

title: Pairing attempt 1 runs before the network is usable (resolv.conf ::1)
description:
On a fresh boot the first pairing attempt fires before DHCP has written /etc/resolv.conf: 'lookup web.whatsapp.com on [::1]:53: connect: cannot assign requested address'. WaitClock passes (the clock is sane) but nothing waits for a usable resolver or a configured interface, so the first attempt always fails and logs a warning that looks like a real fault. Before the QR-handler fix (wat-f2z.8) this failed attempt also poisoned the pairing session.

Consider a netmgr 'network ready' signal (interface up + address + a resolvable DNS server) before the first connect, with the existing retry loop as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: On a cold boot the log shows no failed pairing attempt caused by a missing resolver, or the attempt is retried only after a resolver exists.
close_reason: Fixed and proven on a cold boot of the BeagleBone Black (build of edded8d): 'pairing: waiting for network reason="no interface has an IPv4 address" timeout=15s', then 'network is usable, connecting' after the DHCP lease, then 'connected to WhatsApp'; no [::1]:53 failure. Web UI listening at +14.3 s of boot. AP-mode and loopback-resolver branches remain unit-tested only.
